drug_class: Combination Antiretroviral (HIV medication) — includes an NNRTI and two NRTIs
purpose: This medicine is used to treat HIV (Human Immunodeficiency Virus) in adults and children who weigh at least 40 kg. It helps control the amount of HIV virus in your body so your immune system can stay stronger. It does not cure HIV, but it helps you live a healthier life and lowers the chance of passing HIV to others.
how_it_works: This pill combines three different medicines that each attack HIV in slightly different ways, making it harder for the virus to grow and spread in your body. Two of the medicines (emtricitabine and tenofovir) block a tool the virus needs to copy itself, called reverse transcriptase. The third medicine (efavirenz) also blocks that same tool but works in a different spot, giving you extra protection.
common_side_effects: Dizziness, trouble sleeping, unusual dreams, or feeling lightheaded — especially in the first few weeks. Some people also experience nausea, diarrhea, tiredness, or a rash. The dizziness and strange dreams often get better after 2 to 4 weeks once your body adjusts.
warnings: This medicine can cause serious mood changes, depression, or rarely suicidal thoughts — tell your doctor right away if you feel very down or have thoughts of harming yourself. It can also affect your liver and kidneys, so your doctor will do regular blood tests to monitor these. Do not take it if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant, as it can harm the baby. Avoid alcohol and do not stop taking it suddenly without talking to your doctor first.
typical_dosing: The usual dose is one tablet taken by mouth once a day, on an empty stomach or with a light snack — taking it at bedtime can help reduce dizziness and strange dreams while you sleep. Try to take it at the same time every day, and never skip doses, because missing doses can allow the virus to become resistant to the medicine.
